main_text.l: ta, quamvis sunt fi&ta, possunt arguere
quatuor termini reipsa distincti, in simili-
tudine continuâ sunt quatuor termini ra-
argumentis ortis, quæ fuit in primis, sed
id quod arguunt, sicut prima unde oriun-
tur, quoad essentiam, non quoad modum.
153 Primum illud, vel jugum, quo in-
ter se devincta sunt conjugata, est illud ra-
dicis, quod habent inter se commune.

page.notes: Page is a right-hand page of an early modern book, with a gutter shadow. Several words are blurred and uncertain (e.g. "fi&ta", "diftinctis", "affectio", "ortis", "jugum"); given the image quality, these readings are approximate. Marginal numbers 156 at the foot right are a catchword-like signature and are not transcribed as text. The printed page numbers 145–156 are section numbers, not page numbers.
